name: Wassily Kandinsky
findings: Within his own canvases, dark citrine turns up as a small accent in 40% of the paintings that hold it, 2.2x the archive's rate (from 839 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, dim grey turns up as the lightest note in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 2.3x the archive's rate (from 839 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, brick rose turns up as the shadow in 88% of the paintings that hold it, 3.9x the archive's rate (from 839 paintings here).
Rarely uses dark olive brown, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 839 paintings here).
Rarely uses smoky black, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 839 paintings here).
Pairs chalcedony yellow with primrose yellow more than chance would predict (3 of 839 paintings here).
Pairs liver brown with umber more than chance would predict (3 of 839 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, french grey, greyish white) covers 57% of his paintings here.
